*   `const factory GraphLinkViewGeometry({required Rect bounds, required GraphConnectionGeometry connection, required double thickness, required double angle})`: Creates link geometry.

##### Properties

*   `Rect bounds`: The rectangle spanned by the link's two endpoints. It carries no thickness, so an axis-aligned link has a rect of zero height (or width) — use `containsPoint` rather than `bounds.contains` for hit-testing.
*   `GraphConnectionGeometry connection`: Connection details between nodes.
*   `double thickness`: The thickness of the link. This is the width of the band the user sees and aims at, so it defines the hit area.
*   `double angle`: The angle of the link in radians.

##### Methods

*   `bool containsPoint(Offset point)`: Determines if a point is within the link's area. Rotates the point by `-angle` — laying the link along the x axis whatever its on-screen direction — and tests it against a rect as long as the endpoints are apart and `thickness` wide.

#### GraphConnectionGeometry

Manages geometric relationships between connected nodes.

##### Constructor

*   `const factory GraphConnectionGeometry({required GraphNodeViewGeometry source, required GraphNodeViewGeometry target, required GraphConnectionPoints connectionPoints})`: Creates connection geometry.

##### Properties

*   `GraphNodeViewGeometry source`: Geometry of the source node.
*   `GraphNodeViewGeometry target`: Geometry of the target node.
*   `GraphConnectionPoints connectionPoints`: Specific intersection points.

#### GraphViewGeometry

Tracks graph view layout information (position and size).

##### Constructor

*   `const factory GraphViewGeometry({required Offset position, required Size size})`: Creates view geometry.

##### Properties

*   `Offset position`: Position of the GraphView widget.
*   `Size size`: Size of the GraphView widget.

### Shape Classes

#### GraphShape (Interface)

Interface for defining node shapes in the graph. Provides intersection calculation between a shape and a line, used to determine link connection points.

##### Methods

*   `Set<Offset> getLineIntersections(Rect bounds, GraphLine line)`: Calculates intersection points between this shape (defined by `bounds`) and a `line`. Returns a set of intersection points.

#### GraphCircle

A circular node shape (`GraphShape` implementation).

##### Constructor

*   `const GraphCircle({required double radius})`: Creates a circular shape with a specified `radius`.

##### Properties

*   `double? radius`: The radius of the circle. If null, calculated from bounds.

#### GraphRectangle

A rectangular node shape (`GraphShape` implementation).
Dimensions are determined by the node's bounds passed to `getLineIntersections`.

##### Constructor

*   `const GraphRectangle()`: Creates a rectangular shape.

#### GraphLine

A line segment between two points (`start` and `end`) in the graph's coordinate system. Used internally for intersection calculations.

##### Constructor

*   `const GraphLine(Offset start, Offset end)`: Creates a line.

##### Properties

*   `Offset start`: Starting point.
*   `Offset end`: Ending point.

### Layout Strategies

#### GraphLayoutStrategy

Base class for layout algorithms.

Key implementations:
- `GraphForceDirectedLayoutStrategy`: Physical model-based layout
- `GraphTreeLayoutStrategy`: Hierarchical layout
- `GraphRandomLayoutStrategy`: Random placement
- `GraphManualLayoutStrategy`: Manual positioning

### Debug Interfaces

#### DebugSink

Injection point for structured log telemetry. The core uses the active
`debugSink` to forward per-call log entries to a backend. The default is
`NoopDebugSink` (web-safe, no-op). The real HTTP-backed implementation is
provided by `plough_devtools` and injected via `Plough().attachDebugSink(...)`.

##### Interface

```dart
abstract interface class DebugSink {
  bool get enabled;
  void sendLog({
    required LogCategory category,
    required String level,
    required String message,
    Map<String, dynamic>? metadata,
  });
}
```

##### Implementations

*   `NoopDebugSink`: Default web-safe no-op (always `enabled == false`).
*   `ExternalClientDebugSink` (in `plough_devtools`): HTTP-backed sink that forwards entries to the debug server.

#### DebugBackend

Injection point for advanced debug features (HTTP server, structured logging,
performance monitoring). The default is `NoopDebugBackend`. Injected via
`Plough().attachDebugBackend(...)`.

##### Interface

*   `Future<void> initialize({bool enableServer, bool enableStructuredLogging, bool enablePerformanceMonitoring, int serverPort, bool tryAlternativePorts})`: Starts debug features.
*   `Future<void> shutdown()`: Stops all debug features.
*   `bool get isServerRunning`: Whether the HTTP server is running.
*   `String? get serverUrl`: Server URL, or `null` when not running.
*   `int? get serverPort`: Server port, or `null` when not running.
*   `Map<String, dynamic> generateDebugReport()`: Returns a debug snapshot.

##### Implementations

*   `NoopDebugBackend`: Default web-safe no-op.
*   `DebugManagerBackend` (in `plough_devtools`): Full `dart:io`/`http` server stack.

### Logging API

Top-level logging functions exported from `package:plough/plough.dart`.

*   `bool logEnabled(LogCategory category, [Level? level])`: Returns `true` if a log at `category` (optionally at `level`) would be emitted. Use as a guard before building expensive payloads (maps, joined strings) on hot paths.
*   `void logDebug(LogCategory category, Object message)`: Logs at debug level. `message` may be a `String` or `String Function()` — the closure form avoids string construction when logging is off.
*   `void logInfo(LogCategory category, Object message)`: Logs at info level (same overload as `logDebug`).
*   `void logWarning(LogCategory category, Object message)`: Logs at warning level.
*   `void logError(LogCategory category, Object message)`: Logs at error level.

#### LogCategory (Enum)

Selects the subsystem for a log entry. Used with `logEnabled` and the log functions above.

Values: `gesture`, `selection`, `drag`, `tap`, `layout`, `rendering`, `graph`, `performance`, `debug`, `state`, `animation`, `hitTest`.

### Global Settings

#### Plough (Singleton)

Singleton class managing global settings for the Plough library.
Access the instance via `Plough()`.

The core package ships with web-safe no-op defaults for all debug features.
Advanced debug functionality (HTTP server, structured logging, performance
monitoring) lives in the separate `plough_devtools` package and is injected
at runtime via `attachDebugSink` / `attachDebugBackend`.

##### Properties

*   `bool debugLogEnabled`: Controls the output of debug logs. Setting to `true` enables detailed logging via `configureLogging`.
*   `bool debugViewEnabled`: Controls debug drawing in the graph view (bounding boxes, grid lines, node positions, connection points). Setting to `true` enables `GraphPositionPlotter` globally.
*   `bool debugSignalsEnabled`: Controls the output of debug information related to state management.
*   `bool debugAdvancedEnabled`: Controls the advanced debug backend (server lifecycle). Setting to `true` calls `debugBackend.initialize()`.
*   `String? debugServerUrl`: The running debug server URL (delegates to the active `DebugBackend`; `null` when not running or using the default no-op backend).

##### Methods

*   `Plough enableLogCategories(Map<LogCategory, Level> categories)`: Enable logging for specific categories at specified levels.
*   `Plough enableAllLogCategories([Level level = Level.debug])`: Enable all log categories at the given level.
*   `Plough clearLogCategories()`: Clear all log category configurations.
*   `Future<void> initializeDebugFeatures({bool enableServer, bool enableStructuredLogging, bool enablePerformanceMonitoring, int serverPort, bool tryAlternativePorts})`: Initialize advanced debug features via the active `DebugBackend`.
*   `Future<void> shutdownDebugFeatures()`: Shutdown all debug features via the active `DebugBackend`.
*   `Map<String, dynamic> generateDebugReport()`: Generate a comprehensive debug report snapshot via the active `DebugBackend`.
*   `void attachDebugSink(DebugSink sink)`: Replaces the active `DebugSink` with a custom implementation (e.g. the HTTP-backed sink from `plough_devtools`).
*   `void attachDebugBackend(DebugBackend backend)`: Replaces the active `DebugBackend` with a custom implementation.
*   `void detachDebug()`: Restores the web-safe no-op `DebugSink` and `DebugBackend`.

### Renderer Styles

#### GraphDefaultNodeRendererStyle

Controls node appearance for `GraphDefaultNodeRenderer` with color and dimension options that update based on interaction states.

##### Constructor

*   `const factory GraphDefaultNodeRendererStyle({...})`: Creates a style configuration with numerous optional parameters for colors (normal, hover, selected, highlight), border widths (normal, hover, selected), size (width, height, minWidth, minHeight, radius), and shape.

##### Properties (Examples - see source for all defaults)

*   `Color color`: Background color.
*   `Color borderColor`: Border color.
*   `Color hoverColor`: Background color when hovered.
*   `Color selectedBorderColor`: Border color when selected.
*   `double? radius`: Radius for circular nodes (auto-calculated if null).
*   `double? width`/`height`: Fixed size (auto-calculated if null).
*   `double borderWidth`: Border width in normal state.
*   `double selectedBorderWidth`: Border width when selected.
*   `GraphDefaultNodeRendererShape shape`: Node shape (`circle` or `rectangle`).
*   `EdgeInsets padding`: Padding inside the node's border (defaults to `EdgeInsets.all(8)`). Controls the space between the border and child content.

#### GraphDefaultLinkRendererStyle

Controls link appearance for `GraphDefaultLinkRenderer` with colors and dimensions that update with state changes.

##### Constructor

*   `const factory GraphDefaultLinkRendererStyle({...})`: Creates a style configuration with optional parameters for arrow color, border color, label color, state-specific colors (hover, selected), and arrow size.

##### Properties (Examples - see source for all defaults)

*   `Color arrowColor`: Arrow color.
*   `Color borderColor`: Link line color.
*   `Color hoverColor`: Color when hovered.
*   `Color selectedHoverColor`: Color when selected and hovered.
*   `Size arrowSize`: Size of the arrow.
